kind: simulated-clock real React component / mocked RPC benchmark

methodology.component: Unmodified real baseline and working-tree RemoteSection, with real relative dependencies; only ProxyApi is mocked.
methodology.response: Same online tunnel and one active device for every request in both variants; no user actions or failures.
methodology.boundary: All windows are half-open [start,end): visible/slow [0,60000), hidden [60000,120000), recovered visible [120000,180000). Visibility transitions are registered before mount, so they execute before polling timers at the same timestamp. Requests at 60000 belong only to hidden; at 120000 only to recovered visible; at 180000 excluded. Bootstrap at 0 included.
methodology.initialization: Both mount status and sessions immediately at t=0. Tunnel interval starts only after initial status resolves: first poll at t=2000 fast / t=7000 slow. Sessions cadence is 3000ms; tunnel cadence is 2000ms. Current immediate:false preserves delayed first tunnel poll, but visible recovery polls immediately.
methodology.concurrency: maxInFlight counts outstanding mock RPC promises from recorded start/end events, including combined total and per-method maxima; current single-flight is per polling loop, not global.
methodology.clock: Advance and flush React act every 100ms, not one giant act. All scheduled deadlines in these scenarios align to this grid. Hidden timers are intentionally not browser-throttled, isolating application visibility behavior.
methodology.isolation: Visible -> hidden -> visible is one continuous mounted run per variant. Slow RPC is a separate fresh visible mount with BOTH methods delayed 5000ms including bootstrap. No remount on visibility changes.
methodology.limitations: Not a real browser/mobile-network/battery benchmark. Does not measure HTTP bytes, server CPU, radio wakeups, wall-clock UX, browser background throttling, or cancellation of already in-flight requests.
